start.title: Sons of Adam
start.text:
You open your eyes as the firstborn of Adam and Eve.
A second son, Abel, is born after you.

choices.text: Live as the firstborn son of Adam and Eve
choices.feedback: Genesis 4:1-2 — Eve gave birth to Cain, and then to his brother Abel.

choices.text: Be born before Adam and Eve
choices.feedback: Genesis says Adam and Eve came first; Cain was their son.

choices.text: Grow up as an only child
choices.feedback: Genesis says Cain had a brother, Abel.

fields.title: Your Work
fields.text:
The years pass. Each brother finds his labor.
What is yours?

choices.text: Work the ground as a tiller of the soil
choices.feedback: Genesis 4:2 — Cain worked the soil.

choices.text: Keep flocks of sheep like Abel
choices.feedback: Genesis says Abel kept flocks; Cain worked the soil.

choices.text: Refuse to work at all
choices.feedback: Genesis says Cain worked the ground.

abel_pasture.title: Your Brother's Work
abel_pasture.text:
You see Abel across the field.
What is he doing?

choices.text: See Abel keeping flocks of sheep
choices.feedback: Genesis 4:2 — Abel kept flocks.

choices.text: See Abel tilling the ground beside you
choices.feedback: Genesis says Abel kept flocks, not that he tilled the ground.

choices.text: See Abel fishing at the river
choices.feedback: Genesis does not describe Abel fishing.

offerings.title: Before the Altar
offerings.text:
The time comes to bring an offering to the Lord.
What will you bring?

choices.text: Bring some of the fruits of the soil as an offering
choices.feedback: Genesis 4:3 — Cain brought some of the fruits of the soil as an offering to the Lord.

choices.text: Bring a firstborn lamb from your flock
choices.feedback: Genesis says Abel brought a lamb; Cain brought fruits of the soil.

choices.text: Bring nothing at all
choices.feedback: Genesis says Cain did bring an offering, though not the best.

accepted.title: The Lord's Regard
accepted.text:
You wait as the Lord looks upon the two offerings.
What happens?

choices.text: The Lord looks with favor on Abel and his offering, but not on yours
choices.feedback: Genesis 4:4-5 — The Lord looked with favor on Abel and his offering, but on Cain and his offering He did not look with favor.

choices.text: The Lord favors both offerings equally
choices.feedback: Genesis says the Lord favored Abel's offering, not both.

choices.text: The Lord accepts your offering and rejects Abel's
choices.feedback: Genesis says the opposite — the Lord favored Abel's offering.

anger.title: Your Face Falls
anger.text:
The offering is over. Something rises in you.
How do you respond?

choices.text: Become very angry, your face downcast
choices.feedback: Genesis 4:5 — Cain was very angry, and his face was downcast.

choices.text: Rejoice with Abel over his accepted offering
choices.feedback: Genesis says Cain became angry, not that he rejoiced.

choices.text: Bring a better offering the very next day
choices.feedback: Genesis does not describe Cain bringing a second offering.

warning.title: Sin Crouching at the Door
warning.text:
The Lord speaks to you.
What does He say?

choices.text: 'Sin is crouching at your door — but you must rule over it'
choices.feedback: Genesis 4:6-7 — The Lord warned Cain that sin was crouching at his door and he must rule over it.

choices.text: 'Bring a lamb instead of grain'
choices.feedback: Genesis does not record the Lord telling Cain to bring a lamb.

choices.text: Nothing — the Lord is silent
choices.feedback: Genesis says the Lord did speak to Cain about sin at the door.

invitation.title: You Speak to Your Brother
invitation.text:
Abel walks near, trusting.
What do you say?

choices.text: Say to Abel, 'Let's go out to the field'
choices.feedback: Genesis 4:8 — Cain said to Abel, 'Let's go out to the field.'

choices.text: Invite Abel to worship at the altar together
choices.feedback: Genesis says Cain led Abel out to the field, not to the altar.

choices.text: Send Abel away and never speak to him again
choices.feedback: Genesis says Cain called Abel to the field, not that he sent him away.

field.title: In the Field
field.text:
You and Abel are alone in the open field.
What do you do?

choices.text: Attack Abel your brother and kill him
choices.feedback: Genesis 4:8 — Cain attacked his brother Abel and killed him.

choices.text: Argue with Abel and then forgive him
choices.feedback: Genesis says Cain killed Abel; he did not forgive him.

choices.text: Walk home without touching him
choices.feedback: Genesis says Cain killed Abel in the field.

confrontation.title: "Where Is Your Brother?"
confrontation.text:
The Lord's voice finds you.
"Where is your brother Abel?"

choices.text: Answer: 'I do not know. Am I my brother's keeper?'
choices.feedback: Genesis 4:9 — Cain replied, 'I don't know. Am I my brother's keeper?'

choices.text: Confess plainly: 'I have killed him'
choices.feedback: Genesis says Cain denied knowing; he did not confess plainly.

choices.text: Stay silent before the Lord
choices.feedback: Genesis says Cain answered the Lord; he did not stay silent.

wanderer.title: A Restless Wanderer
wanderer.text:
The Lord places a mark on you for your protection.
You go out to wander east of Eden, in the land of Nod.
